title: Write notes on a primer or plan
html: Signed in, every primer and every learning plan now carries a notes panel — the same one the News page already had, pointed at what you are reading. Write as many as you like, up to 500 characters each, and each one can record which section it is about, so a thought about the habit builder comes back next to the habit builder rather than in a pile. Notes stay private to your account: no other reader sees them, and there is deliberately no page anywhere that lists what people have written. Why sign up sets out what an account does and does not get you. Privacy and Terms were both updated the same day to say that notes now live on primers and plans as well as on news stories.

title: Every note you have written, in one place
html: Notes used to be reachable only where you wrote them, so finding one meant remembering which plan it was on. Your account page now has a Notes tab listing all of them together — news, primers and plans — with a filter for each kind, a link back to whatever the note is about, and the ability to edit, delete, or select several and delete them at once. The Future Skills library shows the count too, on each skill you have written against.

title: Save, pin and note a news story
html: Signed in, every story on the News page now carries three controls. Save as many as you like and they collect behind a Saved filter. Pin exactly one, to hold it at the top of your own list — pinning a second asks first, and tells you which one it would replace. And write a note of up to 500 characters against any story: why it mattered, what you would do about it, who needs to see it. A Has Notes filter brings back everything you have written on. No other account can read your notes, and Privacy is straight about the one limit to that.

title: Every news story has its own page
html: The News page used to be a single page that swapped stories in and out as you clicked. Each story now has its own address, which changes two things worth knowing. A link you share shows that story's own headline and summary in the preview, rather than the site's front page. And the story is in the page itself, so it reads correctly whether or not scripts run. Links shared before the change still work — they now redirect to the story's new address.

title: What's New has its own page
html: This log used to sit in a collapsible block at the foot of the About page. It is now a page of its own, grouped into a card for each month with the most recent one open, and every entry labelled by the kind of change it was.

title: Your learning
html: Your learning is a new page showing how far you are through each skill, with the primer and the plan tracked separately, what you have finished, and what you have not opened yet. Find it in the menu under your avatar, or from the top of the Future Skills library.

title: Mark it complete yourself
html: Every primer and plan now ends with a control to mark it complete — nothing is inferred from how far you scrolled, so it only counts when you say so. Completed items show the date in the sidebar, and you can undo it whenever you like.

title: Accounts, and the pages that explain them
html: Accounts arrived: sign in to keep your place across devices. New privacy & cookies and terms of use pages set out exactly what is stored and why, and why sign up compares an account with browsing as a guest. Account holders can now opt in to hear when new skills or features land.

title: Strategic Synthesis & Decision-Making
html: Added to the library as a new Future Skill, with a primer and full learning plan.

title: Dark mode
html: Toggle light or dark appearance from the nav.

title: Systems Thinking
html: Added to the library as a new Future Skill, with a primer and full learning plan. An announcement banner was added to the homepage for surfacing time-sensitive updates.

title: Search covers News stories
html: Search now indexes individual News stories, not just the News page, and supports extended search with a range of search term operators.

title: News
html: News section added — a curated, dated feed of workforce and skills stories.
